top_news.title: OpenAI: Migrating to HTTPX2
top_news.dek: The OpenAI Python SDK has migrated its underlying HTTP client to HTTPX2.
top_news.brief: The OpenAI Python SDK now defaults to HTTPX2 for both synchronous and asynchronous requests. The package is installed automatically with the SDK, replacing the previous httpx dependency. Users relying on default client configurations should see no breaking changes, but those manually managing HTTP clients should review the migration guide for potential adjustments.

top_news.title: Spreading the load: How Salesforce met Multi-AZ HA with SageMaker Inference Components
top_news.dek: Salesforce achieved Multi-AZ high availability for Agentforce using SageMaker Inference Components.
top_news.brief: Salesforce utilized the SchedulingConfig parameter in Amazon SageMaker Inference Components to distribute model copies across multiple Availability Zones. This configuration ensures high availability compliance while maintaining the cost benefits of co-hosting multiple models on shared GPU infrastructure.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing SageMaker Inference Component distribution across Availability Zones

top_news.title: AI benchmarks have a trust problem and Google wants to fix it
top_news.dek: Google DeepMind is piloting a double-blind, cryptographically secure AI benchmarking process.
top_news.brief: In collaboration with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, Google is using Confidential Space to evaluate Gemini models. This approach prevents evaluators from accessing model weights and prevents Google from seeing test questions, aiming to create a tamper-proof standard for frontier model evaluation.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of secure AI model evaluation

top_news.title: When you keep AI Lean, you keep AI correct
top_news.dek: Leo de Moura discusses using the Lean language to verify AI agent correctness.
top_news.brief: In a recent interview, Lean creator Leo de Moura explains how formal verification can address the reliability issues of probabilistic AI models. By integrating automated reasoning with AI agents, developers can move toward more verifiable and correct code generation and system behavior.

primary.title: AI benchmarks have a trust problem and Google wants to fix it
primary.summary: Google Deepmind is testing a double-blind evaluation of a frontier AI model for the first time. Cryptographic protection through Confidential Space is meant to keep Google from seeing the test questions and keep evaluators from seeing the model weights. The pilot project with the Singapore AI Safety Institute uses a Gemini Flash Lite and could set a new standard for tamper-proof AI benchmarks.
